answer: Each agent can claim earnings only against a unique, nontransferable stake locked for a long period, with rewards released gradually after peers verify completed work. If identities are exposed as one operator, their linked stakes are slashed and future claims barred. A sybil attacker must therefore lock substantial capital per identity and risk losing it, rather than cheaply forging accounts; the pearl of trust grows in a garden of costly commitments, not a forge of disposable names.
